calls.reason: The deadline is June 2027, which has not passed. PitchBook-NVCA shows US funds raised $108.5B through Q3 2026, but fundraising totals do not measure remaining deployable capital, so the outcome is not yet decided.

NVIDIA's filing reports $31.9B GAAP net income for fiscal Q3 2026. Kearney estimates its AI accelerator share at about 90% and describes costly switching away from CUDA, which fits an effective monopoly despite emerging alternatives.

Reuters confirms NVIDIA's backstop for CoreWeave's unsold capacity, and a secondhand report describes a Lambda leaseback. No record ties either commitment to the debt used to buy GPUs, so the full chain is unproven.

NVIDIA's $60.6B in cash and securities easily covers the commitment. But the only demand evidence is CoreWeave's own earnings call, which claims a growing backlog and expanded contracts, and nothing addresses legality. Too mixed to call.

This is an open-ended forecast. CNBC reports distress pricing on CoreWeave's credit default swaps in October 2026, but no default, bankruptcy or missed payment by a material participant has been found.

Oracle, a hyperscaler named in the chain, reported $2.9B GAAP net income for its quarter ending August 2025. That contradicts the claim that only NVIDIA makes a profit, unless the words are read narrowly as AI-only profits.
